source_issues.finding: main.py chirp uses sin(2*pi*f(t)*t), where f(t) is linearly interpolated. Its instantaneous frequency is f0+2*(f1-f0)*t/T, so it does not implement the claimed 200→4000 Hz sweep and aliases at sr=8000. The demo prints sampled frames rather than every frame. Source instructions retained.

Toy pipeline computes magnitude-filterbank features with natural log, while source identifies log(mel_spec + 1e-10) broadly with named models and later acknowledges Whisper has more involved normalization. Do not interpret simplified toy as model-exact preprocessing; source unchanged.

Increasing FFT length alone via zero-padding does not improve true spectral resolution; Hann reduces leakage rather than eliminating it; zero-padded tail frames are not necessarily flat spectra; Hamming endpoints are not zero. Source statements retained.

Keep first 13 coefficients followed by dropping the first leaves 12 unless a replacement is retained. Source does not clarify final count; translation preserves both instructions and does not silently change 13.
Universal 2026/raw-waveform/log-mel/model-table claims and guaranteed WER doubling are overbroad or model/version dependent. No external verification or silent correction performed.

The source chirp computes sin(2*pi*f(t)*t) with linearly increasing f(t), rather than integrating the frequency. Its instantaneous frequency is f0 + 2*(f1-f0)*t/T, so it overshoots the stated 200 to 4000 Hz sweep and aliases at sr=8000. The demo prints selected rather than all frames.

Toy features use magnitude spectra, and code computes log(max(v,eps)), while the explanatory formula says log(v+eps). Named-model frontend equivalence is oversimplified; exact current model preprocessing was not externally audited.

FFT zero-padding alone does not improve true resolution; Hann reduces rather than eliminates leakage; partially zero-padded tail frames need not have flat spectra; Hamming endpoints are nonzero. Source wording is faithfully retained.

Keeping the first 13 coefficients and then dropping the first leaves 12 unless another coefficient is retained. The source gives no final-count clarification; translation correctly keeps both claims and does not silently change 13.

Universal frontend/model-table claims and guaranteed WER doubling are broad, model- and version-sensitive source assertions. No new present-day guarantees were introduced by translation; current model-specific verification remains a separate source task.
